input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.
It’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002. That’s the only one I use.
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?
I checked my phone’s status bar, and it shows the airplane icon. Does that mean my phone is in Airplane Mode? What should I do about this?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode, but now my phone says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?
It says there’s no SIM card detected in my phone. What does that mean? Is something wrong with my phone?

I re-seated the SIM card like you said, and now my phone shows a weak signal and says “2G” with data enabled at the top. Is that good enough to send picture messages, or do I need to do something else?
It says my network mode preference is set to “2G only.” Should I change it to something else? I’m not sure how to do that.
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my phone shows an excellent signal with “5G” and data enabled at the top. Should I try sending a picture message again now?
I tried again, but my messaging app still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? What else can I do?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right—do those look okay to you, or do I need to change something?

I reset the APN settings like you said, but it says they’ll only reset after I reboot my phone. I’m a bit nervous—if I restart my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important.
My phone restarted and the APN settings reset, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON. Also, my messaging app has permission for SMS and phone, but not storage. Should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling and also give the app storage permission? Which one should I do first?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still didn’t work. Should I go ahead and give the messaging app storage permission now?

I granted storage permission to my messaging app, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help—I was really starting to worry. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this doesn’t happen again?

Thank you, that’s very reassuring. I’ll try to remember these tips, but I might need help again if something goes wrong—I get flustered with all these settings! For now, I’m just glad it’s working. Thanks again for your patience and help! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you with that! To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide either your phone number, your full name and date of birth, or your customer ID? This will help me look up your account and assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

Thank you for providing your information. To help you with sending picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things about your service and device. 

Could you please confirm which phone number (line) you are having trouble with, if you have more than one? If you’re not sure, just let me know if it’s the number you provided (555-123-2002) or a different one.
It’s the number I gave you—555-123-2002. That’s the only one I use.

Thank you for confirming. To troubleshoot your issue with sending picture messages, I’ll need you to perform a quick check on your phone. 

Please use your phone to check if you can send MMS messages by running the diagnostic action can_send_mms(). Let me know the result, and I’ll guide you through the next steps based on what you find.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I checked, and it looks like my messaging app cannot send MMS messages right now. What should I do next?

Thank you for checking. Since your messaging app cannot send MMS messages, let’s go through a few steps to identify and resolve the issue. 

First, we need to make sure your phone has both cellular service and mobile data enabled, as both are required for MMS. Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:

- Do you see signal bars (not “No Signal” or “Airplane Mode”)?
- Is there a mobile data icon (like 4G, LTE, 5G, etc.)?

If you’re unsure, you can use the check_status_bar() diagnostic action on your phone and share the results with me. This will help us determine the next step.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I checked my phone’s status bar, and it shows the airplane icon. Does that mean my phone is in Airplane Mode? What should I do about this?

Yes, seeing the airplane icon means your phone is currently in Airplane Mode. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless communications—including cellular service and mobile data—are disabled, which prevents you from sending MMS messages.

To fix this, please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:

1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once Airplane Mode is off, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons reappear. Then, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode, but now my phone says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. Is that normal? What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” indicate that your phone is not currently connected to the cellular network and mobile data is off, which will still prevent you from sending MMS messages.

Let’s troubleshoot further:

1. Please check if your SIM card is properly recognized by your phone. Use the check_sim_status() diagnostic action and let me know what it reports (e.g., Active, Missing, or Locked).
2. If the SIM status is Active, we’ll proceed to enable mobile data. If it’s Missing or Locked, I’ll guide you on what to do next.

Please let me know the result of the SIM status check.
No SIM card detected in the phone.
It says there’s no SIM card detected in my phone. What does that mean? Is something wrong with my phone?

If your phone reports that no SIM card is detected, it usually means the SIM card is either not properly inserted, has shifted out of place, or there’s a temporary connection issue. This is a common cause for having no signal and being unable to send MMS messages.

Here’s what you should do next:

1. Power off your phone.
2. Remove the SIM card tray and carefully take out the SIM card.
3. Reinsert the SIM card, making sure it’s properly seated in the tray.
4. Put the tray back in and power your phone back on.

Alternatively, you can use the reseat_sim_card() action on your device if available.

After doing this, check if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you have signal bars. Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue troubleshooting if needed.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I re-seated the SIM card like you said, and now my phone shows a weak signal and says “2G” with data enabled at the top. Is that good enough to send picture messages, or do I need to do something else?

A “2G” connection is generally not sufficient for sending picture messages (MMS), as MMS requires at least a 3G network connection for reliable delivery.

Let’s try to improve your network connection:

Please check your phone’s network mode preference and make sure it is set to allow 4G or 5G connections. If you can, use the check_network_mode_preference() diagnostic action and let me know what it reports. If it’s set to 2G or 3G only, you’ll need to change it to “4G/5G preferred” or a similar option.

Let me know what your current network mode preference is, and I’ll guide you on how to change it if needed.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only
It says my network mode preference is set to “2G only.” Should I change it to something else? I’m not sure how to do that.

Yes, you should change your network mode preference to allow higher-speed networks, such as 4G or 5G. This will improve your signal quality and enable you to send picture messages (MMS).

Please change your network mode preference to “4G/5G preferred” on your phone. If you’re not sure how to do this, you can use the set_network_mode_preference() action and select “4g_5g_preferred” as the mode.

After you make this change, check if your phone connects to a 4G or 5G network and try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I changed the network mode to “4G/5G preferred,” and now my phone shows an excellent signal with “5G” and data enabled at the top. Should I try sending a picture message again now?

Yes, now that your phone shows an excellent signal with “5G” and data enabled, please try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if the message goes through successfully or if you still encounter any issues. If there’s still a problem, I’ll guide you through the next troubleshooting steps.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I tried again, but my messaging app still can’t send picture messages. This is getting a bit frustrating—why isn’t it working yet? What else can I do?

Thank you for your patience. Since you now have excellent signal and data enabled, but still can’t send picture messages, the next most common cause is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for MMS to work.

Please check your APN settings using the check_apn_settings() diagnostic action on your phone. Let me know if the APN and MMSC URL are set correctly, or if anything looks missing or incorrect. This will help determine if we need to reset your APN settings to fix the issue.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is “internet” and the MMSC URL is “http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc.” I’m not sure if that’s right—do those look okay to you, or do I need to change something?

Thank you for providing your APN settings. The APN name and MMSC URL you shared appear to be in the correct format, but sometimes issues can still occur if there’s a minor error or if the settings have become corrupted.

To ensure your APN settings are correct and up to date, I recommend resetting your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. Please use the reset_apn_settings() action on your phone.

After resetting the APN settings, it’s important to reboot your device for the changes to take effect. Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I reset the APN settings like you said, but it says they’ll only reset after I reboot my phone. I’m a bit nervous—if I restart my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Rest assured, restarting (rebooting) your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or other personal data. A reboot simply turns your phone off and back on, refreshing its system and applying any new settings—like your updated APN configuration.

It’s a safe and common troubleshooting step. Please go ahead and reboot your phone. Once it’s back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works. If you still have trouble, I’ll continue to help you.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
My phone restarted and the APN settings reset, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

Thank you for your patience as we work through this. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, have a strong signal, and data is enabled, let’s check a few more possible causes:

1. Wi-Fi Calling: Sometimes, if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled, it can interfere with MMS. Please check your Wi-Fi Calling status using the check_wifi_calling_status() action. If it’s ON, try turning it OFF and then test sending a picture message again.

2. Messaging App Permissions: The messaging app needs permission to access storage and SMS. Please check your messaging app’s permissions using the check_app_permissions(app_name="messaging") action. If “storage” and “sms” permissions are not granted, please grant them.

Please let me know the results of these checks, and I’ll guide you through any changes needed. We’ll keep working until your issue is resolved!
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
App 'messaging' has permission for: sms, phone.

I checked, and Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON. Also, my messaging app has permission for SMS and phone, but not storage. Should I turn off Wi-Fi Calling and also give the app storage permission? Which one should I do first?

Let’s address both issues, starting with Wi-Fi Calling, as it can directly interfere with MMS delivery:

1. First, please turn OFF Wi-Fi Calling on your phone.
2. After turning off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again.
3. If it still doesn’t work, then grant “storage” permission to your messaging app and try sending the picture message once more.

Let me know the results after each step, and I’ll guide you further if needed.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling and tried sending a picture message again, but it still didn’t work. Should I go ahead and give the messaging app storage permission now?

Yes, please go ahead and grant the “storage” permission to your messaging app. This permission is necessary for the app to access and send picture messages (MMS).

After granting storage permission, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still encounter any issues, and I’ll continue to assist you.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I granted storage permission to my messaging app, and now it looks like I can send picture messages again! Thank you so much for your help—I was really starting to worry. Is there anything else I should do to make sure this doesn’t happen again?

I'm glad to hear that you can send picture messages again! Granting the correct permissions and ensuring your network and device settings are correct usually prevents this issue from recurring.

To help avoid similar problems in the future:
- Keep your messaging app’s permissions for SMS and storage enabled.
- Make sure Airplane Mode is off and your network mode is set to allow 4G/5G.
- If you reset your phone or update your apps, double-check that permissions remain granted.
- If you ever have trouble again, you can repeat these troubleshooting steps or reach out for help.

If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

Thank you, that’s very reassuring. I’ll try to remember these tips, but I might need help again if something goes wrong—I get flustered with all these settings! For now, I’m just glad it’s working. Thanks again for your patience and help! ###STOP###
